high_performing_principles.why_it_works: A visible clash between two clear roles needs no backstory
high_performing_principles.evidence: Short-drama ad teardowns describe plot-driven hooks showing key plot points up front (Insightrackr); directional, vendor analysis
high_performing_principles.best_application: Open on the cruelest line or the physical act, not on the build-up

high_performing_principles.why_it_works: An open question pushes viewers to the app to see the answer
high_performing_principles.evidence: Standard serial-drama practice; episode scripts themselves end on scripted cliffhangers
high_performing_principles.best_application: End one beat before the answer, blow, reveal or decision lands

high_performing_principles.why_it_works: Rags-to-riches / underdog / power-struggle themes are among the most popular
high_performing_principles.evidence: Kuku TV leadership quoted in trade press (afaqs, 2025)
high_performing_principles.best_application: Show the humiliation, then the first sign that the underdog is more powerful; cut before full payoff

weak_or_risky_principles.why_it_underperforms: Nothing in the first 3 s gives a reason to stop scrolling
weak_or_risky_principles.exceptions: A striking image (fire, chains) can work without dialogue

weak_or_risky_principles.why_it_underperforms: No open question means no reason to install or watch
Names, earlier events and flashbacks confuse a first-time viewer
weak_or_risky_principles.exceptions: When one spoken line explains the stakes

hook_rankings: Physical aggression or humiliation on screen (slap, strike, shove, kneel, chains): strongest, needs no context
Shocking accusatory or cruel line delivered face to face
Public betrayal revealed (altar, family turns away)
Identity reveal or recognition ('Who are you?' / 'You already know')
Explicit threat with stakes (execution, arrest, fire)
Emotional reaction shot: only works if the cause is visible in the same 3 s
Mystery question line: weakest alone, pair with visible conflict
retention_findings: By about 10 s a stranger must know who is wronged and by whom
Every 10-15 s should add an escalation or a new turn (rehook); a flat middle loses viewers
30-45 s is the safe length; use 55-60 s only if tension keeps rising
cliffhanger_findings: Strongest: interrupted reveal, sudden arrival or door bursting in, a blow or execution about to happen
Strong: direct question left unanswered, a betrayal just discovered
Weak: a scene fading out on music or ambience, a calm exit, a hug or a resolved argument
microdrama_specific_insights: Short-drama apps mainly advertise with raw clips from their hit shows (AppGrowing on ReelShort)
Ad audiences skew to women aged 25-44 for ReelShort-type romance and revenge drama (AppGrowing)
If the show title already promises the twist (e.g. a secret duke), the reveal is the selling point, not a spoiler
important_tradeoffs: Hook strength vs standalone clarity: the most extreme moment often needs the most context
Spoilers vs payoff: late-episode reveals hook hard but can make episode 1 feel slow

sources.claim: Plot-driven hooks with key plot points up front in short-drama ads
sources.source: Insightrackr, ReelShort Mobile Advertising Intelligence Analysis

DramaBox appears to favour ~1 min ads (single-snapshot caveat)

llm_decision_rules: START on the most charged line or action; never on walking, scenery, or a reaction without its cause
Prefer hooks a stranger reads from roles alone (bride vs groom, maid vs lady) over plot-specific references
Never start mid-sentence or on a line that answers something the viewer did not hear
Inside the first 10 s the wronged person and the wrongdoer must be clear; otherwise standalone <= 3
Score cliffhanger 5 only if the clip ends one beat before an answer, blow, arrival or reveal; ending on resolution <= 2
Each 10-15 s needs a new escalation; flat middles lower the hook and cliffhanger scores
Penalise clips that depend on flashbacks, voice-over, or several unnamed characters
Keep 20-60 s; aim for 30-45 s unless tension keeps rising
Stitched promos must keep the same characters and conflict across segments
Score 5 rarely: at most about 1 in 5 clips deserves it on any dimension
